author: NDT Bureau
title: Xi Jinping Promotes Free Trade During Southeast Asia Tour
text:
• Xi Jinping is touring Southeast Asia, promoting free trade and presenting China as a source of stability.
• He was welcomed in Hanoi by Vietnam’s President Luong Cuong.
• Xi arrived in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, for a three-day visit and will conclude his tour in Cambodia.
• In Hanoi, Xi met with Vietnam’s Communist Party General Secretary To Lam, emphasizing the need for stability in a turbulent world.
• China and Vietnam signed memorandums on cooperation in supply chains and a joint railway project.
• Xi promised greater access for Vietnamese agricultural exports to China, with few details released about the agreements.
• U.S. President Donald Trump criticized the meeting, suggesting China and Vietnam were attempting to undermine the U.S.
• In Malaysia, Xi is expected to discuss a free trade agreement with the 10-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
• ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn stated the agreement would eliminate many tariffs between China and ASEAN members.
• Malaysia hosts several Belt and Road Initiative projects and is China's largest trading partner in the region.
• Xi's tour was likely planned before recent tariff announcements disrupted the global economy.
• The trip allows China to project itself as a responsible superpower amid the impact of U.S. tariffs on Vietnam, Malaysia, and Cambodia.
• Anwar Ibrahim, Malaysia's Prime Minister, has referred to China as a 'true friend' and has visited China multiple times since taking office.
• China's claims in the South China Sea remain contentious with Vietnam and Malaysia, with Anwar asserting Malaysia's right to explore its waters.
